problem_summary.summary: Return the shortest substring of s containing every character required by t, including repeated occurrences; return an empty string if none exists.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: strings s and non-empty t using uppercase and lowercase English letters. Return the unique minimum covering substring or an empty string.
constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters
The answer is unique when it exists

brute_force.explanation: For each start index, extend right while counting characters. Stop at the first endpoint that covers all characters of t, and keep the shortest such window.
brute_force.correctness_idea: For a fixed start, endpoints are considered in increasing order; the first covering endpoint is the shortest valid window from that start. Taking the best across all starts finds the globally shortest covering substring.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(m^2 + 128m) worst case — all starts may scan the remaining string, with fixed-size character-count arrays initialized per start.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — each active start uses arrays of fixed size 128, independent of input length.

optimized.explanation: Keep a frequency array of still-needed characters and a count of missing character occurrences. Expand right until all are covered, then contract left as far as possible while recording the shortest valid window.
optimized.correctness_idea: The missing count decreases only when a newly included character satisfies a still-needed occurrence. When it reaches zero, the window covers t with multiplicity. Contracting left preserves validity until it removes a required occurrence, producing the shortest valid window for that right endpoint. Scanning all right endpoints finds the global minimum.
optimized.time_complexity: O(m + n + 128) — t initializes the frequency table and both window pointers advance at most m times; the fixed alphabet table has 128 entries.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — the frequency table has fixed size 128, excluding the returned substring.

steps.condition: a satisfies one of the two required occurrences.
steps.action: Decrement missing from 2 to 1; the window is not yet valid.

steps.condition: The window aXb now covers both required characters.
steps.action: Record length 3; contract by removing a, which makes the window invalid.

steps.condition: c is not required, so the window still lacks a.
steps.action: Keep scanning; no later endpoint exists, so aXb remains the shortest valid window.

edge_cases.case: No window contains all required characters
edge_cases.handling: The best length remains unset and the method returns an empty string.
The missing count and frequency table track each required occurrence, not just distinct characters.

edge_cases.case: The shortest window is one character
edge_cases.handling: The contraction loop records the one-character window before removing its required character.
Character counts use exact character codes, so letter case is preserved.
